correctness.rationale: The sign-vector incidence order is finite and T0. Every facet vertex of Cm is dominated by any incident original vertex; every original vertex of Ins is dominated by an incident facet. The induced graphs after the respective deletions are complete multipartite graphs with precisely m and 2^(m-1) two-point parts, so their flag complexes are joins of that many 0-spheres. Dowker complex on the 2m minima is the cross-polytope boundary, and Cameron–Kumar Thm 9.2(a) gives both true-nerve homotopy types. The formal graph-domination lemma and all incidence equivalences have been reconstructed in RESULT.md. Script check_incidence.py independently checks m=2,3,4 and exact F2 Betti for m=2,3; finite checks are not the proof of the quantified theorem.

originality.rationale: The closest primary Theorem 9.2(a) covers equivalence of joint-intersection nerves, not clique completions; its Example 9.4 is one smaller contractible-vs-circle instance. The pair of explicit noncontractible spheres with exponentially separated dimensions in a canonical cross-polytope incidence family is not implied by those claims. Dedicated literature-index searches and related-claim comparisons did not show an equivalent or stronger parameter-family result. Unknown alternative hypergraph descriptions remain a noted risk.
residual_risks: Possible earlier characterization of hypergraph two-section intersection complexes or nerve/flag dualities under a different name was not exhaustively searchable; scientific priority is not certified.
The second flag sphere is much larger in dimension than the first; the result is an exact topological classification, not a general equivalence or a theorem about the finite space itself.
The checks performed on an additional flag-complex simple-homotopy reference were abstract-level only.

value.rationale: The recent duality theorem motivates the precise question of what is lost by replacing higher-order common-intersection nerves with clique completions of their visible one-skeleta. A natural infinite family gives both dual flag complexes nontrivial spherical homology in different, exponentially separated dimensions, with exact collapses and a comparison to both genuine nerves. This is a structural boundary for the common graph-approximation procedure, not a small arbitrary numerical enumeration.
